ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points A, O, and B are on the same line, and OC bisects $\angle AOB$. If $\angle COD=28^\circ$ and OE bisects $\angle BOD$, what is the measure of $\angle COE$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that OE bisects $\angle$BOD,\\
it follows that $\angle$DOE = $\frac{1}{2} \angle$BOD = $31^\circ$,\\
hence, $\angle$COE = $\angle$DOE + $\angle$COD = $31^\circ + 28^\circ = \boxed{59^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A, O, B are on the same horizontal straight line, A is on the left side of O, and B is on the right side of O; OC is a vertical ray upward from O; OD and OE are both between OC and OB, and in the direction from OC toward OB, the order is D, E, B. Reasoning: Because OC bisects the straight angle ∠AOB, ∠COB = 90°. It is known that ∠COD = 28°, therefore ∠BOD = 90° - 28° = 62°. Also because OE bisects ∠BOD, ∠DOE = 62° ÷ 2 = 31°. Thus ∠COE = ∠COD + ∠DOE = 28° + 31° = 59°.
